current_example.title: Example: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arcotangent Integral

q-95975.name: Question 1
q-95975.worked_solution:
First, we note that

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}x}{|6x-2|\sqrt{9+(3x-1)^{2}}}=\int \frac{\text{d}x}{6|x-\frac{1}{3}|\sqrt{9+9{(x-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}}}=\frac{1}{18}\int \frac{1}{|x-\frac{1}{3}|\sqrt{1+{(x-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}}}\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=x-\frac{1}{3}.$ Then, we have 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{18}\int \frac{1}{|x-\frac{1}{3}|\sqrt{1+{(x-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{18}\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}}}\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}\operatorname{arcsch}⁡u+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(x-\frac{1}{3})+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(\frac{3x-1}{3})+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Calculate ∫dx|6x−2|9+(3x−1)2.

a
19arsech⁡(3x−13)+C
b
−19arcsch⁡(3x−1)+C
c
−118arcsch⁡(3x−13)+C
d
−118arsech⁡(3x−13)+C
e
118arcsch⁡(3x−1)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that ∫dx|6x−2|9+(3x−1)2=∫dx6|x−13|9+9(x−13)2=118∫1|x−13|1+(x−13)2dx.

Let u=x−13. Then, we have dudx=1⟹dx=du.

Therefore, 118∫1|x−13|1+(x−13)2dx=118∫1|u|1+u2du=−118arcsch⁡u+C=−118arcsch⁡(x−13)+C=−118arcsch⁡(3x−13)+C.

q-97313.name: Question 2
q-97313.worked_solution:
First, we note that

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}x}{(6x-4)\sqrt{9-(3x-2)^{2}}}=\int \frac{\text{d}x}{6(x-\frac{2}{3})\sqrt{9-9{(x-\frac{2}{3})}^{2}}}=\frac{1}{18}\int \frac{1}{(x-\frac{2}{3})\sqrt{1-{(x-\frac{2}{3})}^{2}}}\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=x-\frac{2}{3}.$ Then, we have 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{18}\int \frac{1}{(x-\frac{2}{3})\sqrt{1-{(x-\frac{2}{3})}^{2}}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{18}\int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}\operatorname{arsech}⁡u+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}\operatorname{arsech}⁡(x-\frac{2}{3})+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}\operatorname{arsech}⁡(\frac{3x-2}{3})+C.\end{aligned}
$$

q-97313.knowledge_point: Computing an Inverse Reciprocal Hyperbolic Integral Containing a Completed Square

q-97758.name: Question 3
q-97758.worked_solution:
First, we note that

$$
\int \frac{1}{4-(x+3)^{2}}\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{4-4{(\frac{x+3}{2})}^{2}}\text{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{x+3}{2})}^{2}}\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=\frac{x+3}{2}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=2\,\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{x+3}{2})}^{2}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\cdot 2\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(\frac{x+3}{2})+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that this result is subject to the condition $|\frac{x+3}{2}|>1.$

q-97758.html:
Question 3
?

Calculate ∫14−(x+3)2dx.

a
12arcoth⁡(x+32)+C
b
12arcoth⁡(x+32)+C
c
14arcoth⁡(x+32)+C
d
2arcoth⁡(x+32)+C
e
14arcoth⁡(x+32)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that ∫14−(x+3)2dx=∫14−4(x+32)2dx=14∫11−(x+32)2dx.

Let u=x+32. Then, we have dudx=12⟹dx=2du.

Therefore, 14∫11−(x+32)2dx=14∫11−u2⋅2du=12∫11−u2du=12⋅arcoth⁡u+C=12arcoth⁡(x+32)+C.

Note that this result is subject to the condition |x+32|>1.
q-97758.knowledge_point: Computing an Inverse Reciprocal Hyperbolic Integral Containing a Completed Square

q-97750.name: Question 4
q-97750.worked_solution:
First, we note that

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}x}{(x+1)\sqrt{9-(3x+3)^{2}}} & =\int \frac{\text{d}x}{(x+1)\sqrt{9-9{(x+1)}^{2}}}=\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{(x+1)\sqrt{1-(x+1)^{2}}}\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u=x+1.$ Then, we have 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{(x+1)\sqrt{1-(x+1)^{2}}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arsech}⁡u+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arsech}⁡(x+1)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Calculate ∫dx(x+1)9−(3x+3)2.

a
16arcsch⁡(3x+1)+C
b
3arcsch⁡(x+1)+C
c
−13arsech⁡(3x+1)+C
d
−13arsech⁡(x+1)+C
e
−16arsech⁡(x+1)+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we note that

∫dx(x+1)9−(3x+3)2=∫dx(x+1)9−9(x+1)2=13∫1(x+1)1−(x+1)2dx.

Let u=x+1. Then, we have

dudx=1⟹dx=du.

Therefore, 13∫1(x+1)1−(x+1)2dx=13∫1u1−u2⋅du=−13arsech⁡u+C=−13arsech⁡(x+1)+C.

q-95973.name: Question 5
q-95973.worked_solution:
First, we note that

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}x}{(x-1)\sqrt{4-(2x-2)^{2}}} & =\int \frac{\text{d}x}{(x-1)\sqrt{4-4{(x-1)}^{2}}}=\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{(x-1)\sqrt{1-(x-1)^{2}}}\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u=x-1.$ Then, we have 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{(x-1)\sqrt{1-(x-1)^{2}}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arsech}⁡u+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arsech}⁡(x-1)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95973.html:
Question 5
?

Calculate ∫dx(x−1)4−(2x−2)2.

a
14arsech⁡(x−1)+C
b
−12arsech⁡(x−1)+C
c
14arcsch⁡(2x−2)+C
d
−12arsech⁡(2x−1)+C
e
2arcsch⁡(x−1)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that

∫dx(x−1)4−(2x−2)2=∫dx(x−1)4−4(x−1)2=12∫1(x−1)1−(x−1)2dx.

Let u=x−1. Then, we have

dudx=1⟹dx=du.

Therefore, 12∫1(x−1)1−(x−1)2dx=12∫1u1−u2⋅du=−12arsech⁡u+C=−12arsech⁡(x−1)+C.
q-95973.knowledge_point: Computing an Inverse Reciprocal Hyperbolic Integral Containing a Completed Square

q-97776.name: Question 6
q-97776.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+2x+4 & =-({x}^{2}-2x-4) \\  & =-({x}^{2}-2\cdot x+{1}^{2}-{1}^{2}-4) \\  & =-((x-1)^{2}-5) \\  & =5-(x-1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\sqrt{5}}{(x-1)\sqrt{4+2x-{x}^{2}}} & =\int \frac{\sqrt{5}}{(x-1)\sqrt{5-{(x-1)}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{(\frac{x-1}{\sqrt{5}})\sqrt{5-5{(\frac{x-1}{\sqrt{5}})}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\int \frac{1}{(\frac{x-1}{\sqrt{5}})\sqrt{1-{(\frac{x-1}{\sqrt{5}})}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u=\frac{x-1}{\sqrt{5}}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\sqrt{5}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\sqrt{5}}{(x-1)\sqrt{4+2x-{x}^{2}}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\int \frac{1}{(\frac{x-1}{\sqrt{5}})\sqrt{1-{(\frac{x-1}{\sqrt{5}})}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\cdot \sqrt{5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\operatorname{arsech}⁡u+C \\  & =-\operatorname{arsech}⁡(\frac{x-1}{\sqrt{5}})+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-97776.html:
Question 6
?

∫5(x−1)4+2x−x2dx=

a
−arsech⁡(x−15)+C
b
15arcsch⁡(x−15)+C
c
−15arsech⁡(x−15)+C
d
−5arsech⁡(x−15)+C
e
arcsch⁡(x−15)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator: −x2+2x+4=−(x2−2x−4)=−(x2−2⋅x+12−12−4)=−((x−1)2−5)=5−(x−1)2

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get ∫5(x−1)4+2x−x2=∫5(x−1)5−(x−1)2dx=∫1(x−15)5−5(x−15)2dx=15∫1(x−15)1−(x−15)2dx.

Let u=x−15. Then, we have dudx=15⟹dx=5du.

Therefore,

∫5(x−1)4+2x−x2dx=15∫1(x−15)1−(x−15)2dx=15∫1u1−u2⋅5du=∫1u1−u2du=−arsech⁡u+C=−arsech⁡(x−15)+C.
q-97776.knowledge_point: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arsecant Integral

q-97766.name: Question 7
q-97766.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4{x}^{2}-8x & =-4({x}^{2}+2x) \\  & =-4({x}^{2}+2\cdot x+{1}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =-4[(x+1)^{2}-1] \\  & =4[1-(x+1)^{2}]\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{(x+1)\sqrt{-4{x}^{2}-8x}}\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{(x+1)\sqrt{4[1-(x+1)^{2}]}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{(x+1)\sqrt{1-(x+1)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=x+1.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{(x+1)\sqrt{-4{x}^{2}-8x}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{(x+1)\sqrt{1-(x+1)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arsech}⁡u+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arsech}⁡(x+1)+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-97766.html:
Question 7
?

∫1(x+1)−4x2−8xdx=

a
−4arsech⁡(x+1)+C
b
−12arsech⁡(x+1)+C
c
−14arsech⁡(x+1)+C
d
−12arcsch⁡(x+1)+C
e
12arcsch⁡(x+1)+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator: −4x2−8x=−4(x2+2x)=−4(x2+2⋅x+12−12)=−4[(x+1)2−1]=4[1−(x+1)2]

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get ∫1(x+1)−4x2−8xdx=∫1(x+1)4[1−(x+1)2]dx=12∫1(x+1)1−(x+1)2dx.

Let u=x+1. Then, we have dudx=1⟹dx=du.

Therefore,

∫1(x+1)−4x2−8xdx=12∫1(x+1)1−(x+1)2dx=12∫1u1−u2du=−12arsech⁡u+C=−12arsech⁡(x+1)+C.
q-97766.knowledge_point: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arsecant Integral

q-95976.name: Question 8
q-95976.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}-4x-3 & =-({x}^{2}+4x+3) \\  & =-({x}^{2}+2\cdot 2x+{2}^{2}-{2}^{2}+3) \\  & =-((x+2)^{2}-1) \\  & =1-(x+2)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{(x+2)\sqrt{-{x}^{2}-4x-3}}\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{(x+2)\sqrt{1-(x+2)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=x+2.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{(x+2)\sqrt{-{x}^{2}-4x-3}}\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{(x+2)\sqrt{1-(x+2)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\text{d}u \\  & =-\operatorname{arsech}⁡u+C \\  & =-\operatorname{arsech}⁡(x+2)+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

∫1(x+2)−x2−4x−3dx=

a
−12arcsch⁡(x+2)+C
b
−12arsech⁡(x+2)+C
c
arcsch⁡(x+2)+C
d
−arsech⁡(x+2)+C
e
−2arsech⁡(x+2)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator: −x2−4x−3=−(x2+4x+3)=−(x2+2⋅2x+22−22+3)=−((x+2)2−1)=1−(x+2)2

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get ∫1(x+2)−x2−4x−3dx=∫1(x+2)1−(x+2)2dx.

Let u=x+2. Then, we have dudx=1⟹dx=du.

Therefore,

∫1(x+2)−x2−4x−3dx=∫1(x+2)1−(x+2)2dx=∫1u1−u2du=−arsech⁡u+C=−arsech⁡(x+2)+C.

q-97778.name: Question 9
q-97778.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+10x-24 & =-({x}^{2}-10x+24) \\  & =-({x}^{2}-2\cdot 5x+{5}^{2}-{5}^{2}+24) \\  & =-((x-5)^{2}-1) \\  & =1-(x-5)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{(3x-15)\sqrt{10x-{x}^{2}-24}}\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{(x-5)\sqrt{1-(x-5)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=x-5.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{(3x-15)\sqrt{10x-{x}^{2}-24}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{(x-5)\sqrt{1-(x-5)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arsech}⁡u+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arsech}⁡(x-5)+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-97762.name: Question 10
q-97762.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-{x}^{2}-3 & =-({x}^{2}-4x+3) \\  & =-({x}^{2}-2\cdot 2x+{2}^{2}-{2}^{2}+3) \\  & =-((x-2)^{2}-1) \\  & =1-(x-2)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{(x-2)\sqrt{4x-{x}^{2}-3}}\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{(x-2)\sqrt{1-(x-2)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=x-2.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{(x-2)\sqrt{4x-{x}^{2}-3}}\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{(x-2)\sqrt{1-(x-2)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\text{d}u \\  & =-\operatorname{arsech}⁡u+C \\  & =-\operatorname{arsech}⁡(x-2)+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-97762.html:
Question 10
?

∫1(x−2)4x−x2−3dx=

a
arcsch⁡(x−2)+C
b
−4arsech⁡(x−2)+C
c
−14arsech⁡(x−2)+C
d
−arsech⁡(x−2)+C
e
−12arcsch⁡(x−2)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator: 4x−x2−3=−(x2−4x+3)=−(x2−2⋅2x+22−22+3)=−((x−2)2−1)=1−(x−2)2

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get ∫1(x−2)4x−x2−3dx=∫1(x−2)1−(x−2)2dx.

Let u=x−2. Then, we have dudx=1⟹dx=du.

Therefore,

∫1(x−2)4x−x2−3dx=∫1(x−2)1−(x−2)2dx=∫1u1−u2du=−arsech⁡u+C=−arsech⁡(x−2)+C.
q-97762.knowledge_point: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arsecant Integral

q-97781.name: Question 11
q-97781.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{x}^{2}+6x+10 & =9({x}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}x+\frac{10}{9}) \\  & =9({x}^{2}+2\cdot \frac{1}{3}x+{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+\frac{10}{9}) \\  & =9[{(x+\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+1]\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3}{|3x+1|\sqrt{9{x}^{2}+6x+10}}\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{|x+\frac{1}{3}|\sqrt{9[1+{(x+\frac{1}{3})}^{2}]}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{|x+\frac{1}{3}|\sqrt{1+{(x+\frac{1}{3})}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u=x+\frac{1}{3}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{|x+\frac{1}{3}|\sqrt{1+{(x+\frac{1}{3})}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arcsch}⁡u+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(x+\frac{1}{3})+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

∫3|3x+1|9x2+6x+10dx=

a
−19arcsch⁡(x+13)+C
b
−3arcsch⁡(x+13)+C
c
−13arcsch⁡(x+13)+C
d
3arsech⁡(x+13)+C
e
13arsech⁡(x+13)+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

9x2+6x+10=9(x2+23x+109)=9(x2+2⋅13x+(13)2−(13)2+109)=9[(x+13)2+1]

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get ∫3|3x+1|9x2+6x+10dx=∫1|x+13|9[1+(x+13)2]dx=13∫1|x+13|1+(x+13)2dx.

Let u=x+13. Then, we have dudx=1⟹dx=du.

Therefore,

13∫1|x+13|1+(x+13)2dx=13∫1|u|1+u2du=−13arcsch⁡u+C=−13arcsch⁡(x+13)+C.
q-97781.knowledge_point: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arcosecant Integral

q-97903.name: Question 12
q-97903.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}+4x+5 & =4({x}^{2}+x+\frac{5}{4}) \\  & =4({x}^{2}+2\cdot \frac{1}{2}x+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+\frac{5}{4}) \\  & =4[{(x+\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+1]\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{|2x+1|\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+4x+5}}\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{|x+\frac{1}{2}|\sqrt{4[1+{(x+\frac{1}{2})}^{2}]}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{|x+\frac{1}{2}|\sqrt{1+{(x+\frac{1}{2})}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u=x+\frac{1}{2}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{|x+\frac{1}{2}|\sqrt{1+{(x+\frac{1}{2})}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arcsch}⁡u+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(x+\frac{1}{2})+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-97903.html:
Question 12
?

∫2|2x+1|4x2+4x+5dx=

a
−12arcsch⁡(x+12)+C
b
−2arsech⁡(x+12)+C
c
−14arcsch⁡(x+12)+C
d
12arsech⁡(x+12)+C
e
−2arcsch⁡(x+12)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

4x2+4x+5=4(x2+x+54)=4(x2+2⋅12x+(12)2−(12)2+54)=4[(x+12)2+1]

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get ∫2|2x+1|4x2+4x+5dx=∫1|x+12|4[1+(x+12)2]dx=12∫1|x+12|1+(x+12)2dx.

Let u=x+12. Then, we have dudx=1⟹dx=du.

Therefore,

12∫1|x+12|1+(x+12)2dx=12∫1|u|1+u2du=−12arcsch⁡u+C=−12arcsch⁡(x+12)+C.

q-97901.name: Question 13
q-97901.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+6x+13 & ={x}^{2}+2\cdot 3x+{3}^{2}-{3}^{2}+13 \\  & =(x+3)^{2}+4\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -\frac{6}{|x+3|\sqrt{{x}^{2}+6x+13}}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \frac{6}{|x+3|\sqrt{4+(x+3)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{6}{2|\frac{x+3}{2}|\sqrt{4+4{(\frac{x+3}{2})}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{1}{|\frac{x+3}{2}|\sqrt{1+{(\frac{x+3}{2})}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u=\frac{x+3}{2}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=2\,\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{1}{|\frac{x+3}{2}|\sqrt{1+{(\frac{x+3}{2})}^{2}}}\text{d}x & =-\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}}}\cdot 2\,\text{d}u \\  & =-3\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{arcsch}⁡u+C \\  & =3\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(\frac{x+3}{2})+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-95977.name: Question 14
q-95977.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4x+5 & ={x}^{2}-2\cdot 2x+{2}^{2}-{2}^{2}+5 \\  & =(x-2)^{2}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{2}{|4x-8|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-4x+5}}\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{2}{4|x-2|\sqrt{1+(x-2)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{|x-2|\sqrt{1+(x-2)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=x-2.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{|x-2|\sqrt{1+(x-2)^{2}}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arcsch}⁡u+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(x-2)+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

∫2|4x−8|x2−4x+5dx=

a
−12arsech⁡(x−2)+C
b
12arsech⁡(x−2)+C
c
−2arcsch⁡(x−2)+C
d
−12arcsch⁡(x−2)+C
e
2arsech⁡(x−2)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

x2−4x+5=x2−2⋅2x+22−22+5=(x−2)2+1

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get ∫2|4x−8|x2−4x+5dx=∫24|x−2|1+(x−2)2dx=12∫1|x−2|1+(x−2)2dx.

Let u=x−2. Then, we have dudx=1⟹dx=du.

Therefore,

12∫1|x−2|1+(x−2)2dx=12∫1|u|1+u2du=−12arcsch⁡u+C=−12arcsch⁡(x−2)+C.
q-95977.knowledge_point: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arcosecant Integral

q-97780.name: Question 15
q-97780.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2x+5 & ={x}^{2}+2\cdot x+{1}^{2}-{1}^{2}+5 \\  & =(x+1)^{2}+4\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4}{|x+1|\sqrt{{x}^{2}+2x+5}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{4}{|x+1|\sqrt{4+(x+1)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2}{|\frac{x+1}{2}|\sqrt{4+4{(\frac{x+1}{2})}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{|\frac{x+1}{2}|\sqrt{1+{(\frac{x+1}{2})}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u=\frac{x+1}{2}.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=2\,\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{|\frac{x+1}{2}|\sqrt{1+{(\frac{x+1}{2})}^{2}}}\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}}}\cdot 2\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-2\operatorname{arcsch}⁡u+C \\  & =-2\operatorname{arcsch}⁡(\frac{x+1}{2})+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-97780.html:
Question 15
?

∫4|x+1|x2+2x+5dx=

a
−2arcsch⁡(x+12)+C
b
12arsech⁡(x+12)+C
c
−12arcsch⁡(x+12)+C
d
−4arcsch⁡(x+12)+C
e
2arsech⁡(x+12)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the argument of the square root in the denominator:

x2+2x+5=x2+2⋅x+12−12+5=(x+1)2+4

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get ∫4|x+1|x2+2x+5dx=∫4|x+1|4+(x+1)2dx=∫2|x+12|4+4(x+12)2dx=∫1|x+12|1+(x+12)2dx.

Let u=x+12. Then, we have dudx=12⟹dx=2du.

Therefore,

∫1|x+12|1+(x+12)2dx=∫1|u|1+u2⋅2du=2∫1|u|1+u2du=−2arcsch⁡u+C=−2arcsch⁡(x+12)+C.
q-97780.knowledge_point: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arcosecant Integral

q-95979.name: Question 16
q-95979.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-4x-{x}^{2} & =-({x}^{2}+4x-1) \\  & =-({x}^{2}+2\cdot 2x+{2}^{2}-{2}^{2}-1) \\  & =-((x+2)^{2}-5) \\  & =5-(x+2)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the denominator of our integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{1-4x-{x}^{2}}\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{5-(x+2)^{2}}\text{d}x=\frac{1}{5}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(x+2))}^{2}}\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(x+2).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\sqrt{5}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(x+2))}^{2}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{5}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(x+2))+C \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(\frac{x+2}{\sqrt{5}})+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that this result is subject to the condition $|\frac{x+2}{\sqrt{5}}|>1.$

Question 16
?

∫11−4x−x2dx=

a
15arcoth⁡(x+25)+C
b
−15arcoth⁡(x+25)+C
c
15arcoth⁡(x+25)+C
d
−55arcoth⁡(x+25)+C
e
55arcoth⁡(x+25)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the denominator: 1−4x−x2=−(x2+4x−1)=−(x2+2⋅2x+22−22−1)=−((x+2)2−5)=5−(x+2)2

Substituting the above into the denominator of our integral, we get ∫11−4x−x2dx=∫15−(x+2)2dx=15∫11−(15(x+2))2dx.

Let u=15(x+2). Then, we have dudx=15⟹dx=5du.

Therefore, 15∫11−(15(x+2))2dx=15∫11−u2⋅5du=55∫11−u2du=55⋅arcoth⁡u+C=55⋅arcoth⁡(15(x+2))+C=55arcoth⁡(x+25)+C.

Note that this result is subject to the condition |x+25|>1.

q-95978.name: Question 17
q-95978.worked_solution:
First, we note that

$$
\int \frac{1}{9-(x+4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{9-9(\frac{1}{9}(x+4)^{2})}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{9}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{1}{3}(x+4))}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=\frac{1}{3}(x+4).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{3}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=3\,\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{9}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{1}{3}(x+4))}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{9}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\,\cdot 3\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{9}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(\frac{x+4}{3})+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that this result is subject to the condition $|\frac{x+4}{3}|>1.$

q-97907.name: Question 18
q-97907.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-{x}^{2}-5 & =-({x}^{2}-6x+5) \\  & =-({x}^{2}-2\cdot 3x+{3}^{2}-{3}^{2}+5) \\  & =-((x-3)^{2}-4) \\  & =4-(x-3)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the denominator of our integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{6x-{x}^{2}-5}\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{4-(x-3)^{2}}\text{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{1}{2}(x-3))}^{2}}\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=\frac{1}{2}(x-3).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=2\,\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{1}{2}(x-3))}^{2}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\cdot 2\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡(\frac{1}{2}(x-3))+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(\frac{x-3}{2})+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that this result is subject to the condition $|\frac{x-3}{2}|>1.$

q-97907.html:
Question 18
?

∫16x−x2−5dx=

a
22arcoth⁡(x−32)+C
b
22arcoth⁡(x−32)+C
c
12arcoth⁡(x−32)+C
d
−22arcoth⁡(x−32)+C
e
−12arcoth⁡(x−32)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the denominator: 6x−x2−5=−(x2−6x+5)=−(x2−2⋅3x+32−32+5)=−((x−3)2−4)=4−(x−3)2

Substituting the above into the denominator of our integral, we get ∫16x−x2−5dx=∫14−(x−3)2dx=14∫11−(12(x−3))2dx.

Let u=12(x−3). Then, we have dudx=12⟹dx=2du.

Therefore, 14∫11−(12(x−3))2dx=14∫11−u2⋅2du=12∫11−u2du=12⋅arcoth⁡u+C=12⋅arcoth⁡(12(x−3))+C=12arcoth⁡(x−32)+C.

Note that this result is subject to the condition |x−32|>1.
q-97907.knowledge_point: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arcotangent Integral

q-98008.name: Question 19
q-98008.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}12x-{x}^{2}-33 & =-({x}^{2}-12x+33) \\  & =-({x}^{2}-2\cdot 6x+{6}^{2}-{6}^{2}+33) \\  & =-((x-6)^{2}-3) \\  & =3-(x-6)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the denominator of our integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{12x-{x}^{2}-33}\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{3-(x-6)^{2}}\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(x-6))}^{2}}\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(x-6).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\sqrt{3}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(x-6))}^{2}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(x-6))+C \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(\frac{x-6}{\sqrt{3}})+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that this result is subject to the condition $|\frac{x-6}{\sqrt{3}}|>1.$

Question 19
?

∫112x−x2−33dx=

a
13arcoth⁡(x−63)+C
b
33arcoth⁡(x−63)+C
c
−33arcoth⁡(x−63)+C
d
−13arcoth⁡(x−63)+C
e
13arcoth⁡(x−63)+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the denominator: 12x−x2−33=−(x2−12x+33)=−(x2−2⋅6x+62−62+33)=−((x−6)2−3)=3−(x−6)2

Substituting the above into the denominator of our integral, we get ∫112x−x2−33dx=∫13−(x−6)2dx=13∫11−(13(x−6))2dx.

Let u=13(x−6). Then, we have dudx=13⟹dx=3du.

Therefore, 13∫11−(13(x−6))2dx=13∫11−u2⋅3du=33∫11−u2du=33⋅arcoth⁡u+C=33⋅arcoth⁡(13(x−6))+C=33arcoth⁡(x−63)+C.

Note that this result is subject to the condition |x−63|>1.
q-98008.knowledge_point: Completing the Square to Compute a Hyperbolic Arcotangent Integral

q-98005.name: Question 20
q-98005.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}12+4x-{x}^{2} & =-({x}^{2}-4x-12) \\  & =-({x}^{2}-2\cdot 2x+{2}^{2}-{2}^{2}-12) \\  & =-((x-2)^{2}-16) \\  & =16-(x-2)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the denominator of our integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{12+4x-{x}^{2}}\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{16-(x-2)^{2}}\text{d}x=\frac{1}{16}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{1}{4}(x-2))}^{2}}\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=\frac{1}{4}(x-2).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{4}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=4\,\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{16}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{1}{4}(x-2))}^{2}}\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{16}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\cdot 4\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \operatorname{arcoth}⁡(\frac{1}{4}(x-2))+C \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(\frac{x-2}{4})+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that this result is subject to the condition $|\frac{x-2}{4}|>1.$

q-98005.html:
Question 20
?

∫112+4x−x2dx=

a
18arcoth⁡(x−24)+C
b
14arcoth⁡(x−22)+C
c
14arcoth⁡(x−24)+C
d
116arcoth⁡(x−24)+C
e
−116arcoth⁡(x−22)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we complete the square for the denominator: 12+4x−x2=−(x2−4x−12)=−(x2−2⋅2x+22−22−12)=−((x−2)2−16)=16−(x−2)2

Substituting the above into the denominator of our integral, we get ∫112+4x−x2dx=∫116−(x−2)2dx=116∫11−(14(x−2))2dx.

Let u=14(x−2). Then, we have dudx=14⟹dx=4du.

Therefore, 116∫11−(14(x−2))2dx=116∫11−u2⋅4du=14∫11−u2du=14⋅arcoth⁡u+C=14⋅arcoth⁡(14(x−2))+C=14arcoth⁡(x−24)+C.

Note that this result is subject to the condition |x−24|>1.
